program: Ordinary-gift expected health: dental, counseling, hypertension and residual care
eyebrow: SAN FRANCISCO · WHOLE-GIFT · EXPLICIT SUBJECTIVE EXPECTATION

nutshell.headline: Our expected ordinary-gift estimate includes major medical care, not just selected extractions.
nutshell.body: For a $100,000 ordinary gift, our subjective expected donor cost per 10 QALYs is $2,002,578 across all recipients, $2,002,578 in the Bay Area and $2,860,825 in SF. Expected gross associated resource prices are $3,967,448, $3,967,448 and $5,667,783 respectively. This averages signed health across explicitly weighted scenarios (70% central,15% favorable,10% cautious,5% no additional funding), not positive-only ratios. It adds selected hypertension care and uncertain residual morbidity to dental relief and counseling. The unweighted central SF donor scenario is $11,395,651. These are weak, judgment-heavy best estimates, not measured clinic impact or confidence bounds.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Sustained treatment of hypertension can reduce mortality; dental, mental and other medical care can bring symptom/function improvement sooner.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Gift allocation and named service-mix priors are unobserved locally. Favorable15% supplies 82.6%of expectedQ; zero favorable weight raises expected SF donor price to$13,517,426.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Validate ordinary-gift service capacity, patient mix and current-care contrast; measure utilities and linked unique outcomes. Use expectation-weight and residual-null sensitivities before treating the ranking as robust.

summary.label: SUBJECTIVE EXPECTED — SF
summary.detail: Whole gift divided by expected signed direct SF QALYs; weak scenario-weight priors.

summary.label: EXPECTED GROSS RESOURCES — SF
summary.detail: Ratio of expected gross associated costs to expected health; not full net societal ICER.

summary.label: CENTRAL SCENARIO — SF
summary.detail: Not equal to expectation; favorable tail materially affects mean.

summary.label: FUNDING ROOM
summary.detail: Capacity and displacement are explicit priors, not a priced additional-care offer.

programSection.body: Clinic by the Bay is Volunteers in Medicine – San Francisco, EIN 26-2593712. It supplies free medical, dental, mental-health and food-pharmacy services. Dental access requires being an active medical patient; exams, cleaning and prevention are not completed pain treatment. Its current dental scope includes simple fillings/extractions but not root canals or tooth replacement. Counseling is short-term; psychiatry is monthly. The organization reports no government or insurance receipts, but public and other free-care alternatives remain relevant. The medical model now includes a selected hypertensive annual-care cohort and an explicit uncertain residual person-course model for the other health-bearing activities.

steps.title: Fund the full portfolio
steps.detail: Retain all $100K:20%dental,15%mental,55%medical,10%food/other, including allocated support. BP courses use30% of medical spending centrally. Remaining budget after selected dental/counseling/BP course shares enters the residual model; no second spending allocation is added.

steps.title: Count distinct annual patient courses
steps.detail: One patient-period ledger assigns dental, counseling, BP then residual. Unique fractions explicitly remove overlap and repeats. These are priors; downstream effects must be reconciled before combining other organizations.

steps.title: Model finite clinical effects and residual uncertainty
steps.detail: BP survival differs only during funded effective care after latency; equal hazards afterward to10year horizon. Six named residual service groups each have distinct course cost, target/response, signed utility and finite catchup/horizon: acute/rheumatology, non-BP medication care, completed referrals, other dental, other mental, and food support.

programSection.boundary: Whole-gift expected direct-health model with four explicit branches. Residual aggregate priors are much weaker than trial-anchored BP evidence. Rare preventive tails and indirect effects remain unresolved rather than asserted absent; sensitivity must expose their possible materiality. SF nests within Bay, not an additive second population.

model.headline: $2,860,825 expected donor dollars per 10 direct SF QALYs
model.body: Central components: dental0.03478304880Q; counseling0.009869798320; BP0.01690422578; six residual groups together0.06380403741. BP uses HDFP assignment-level systematic-care versus community-referral evidence, not untreated all-visits effects. Six group-specific residual priors replace the generic uplift; service availability is sourced, but numeric illness mix and utility are explicitly weak judgments. Non-BP medical spending splits40%acute/rheumatology,40%other symptomatic chronic medication care and20%completed specialty pathways. Each cohort is counted once.

equation.label: EXPECTED FULL-GIFT PRICE
equation.expression: Q=Q_dental+Q_counseling+Q_BP+Σ_g N_g[target_g×response_g×signed utility_g×discount(delay)×F(catchup_g+m+r,H_g)−harm]−independent harm; N_g is unique additional patient-courses from its partitioned whole-gift budget, capped jointly; E[Q]=Σscenario w_i×signed Q_i; donor price=10G/E[Q_SF], only if positive.

inputs.label: gift usd
inputs.basis: Hypothetical ordinary unrestricted gift; not a quoted tranche.

inputs.label: funding additionality
inputs.basis: Fraction expanding or preserving otherwise-lost care after replacement of existing donors; distinct from alternative care after treatment starts.

inputs.label: dental allocation
inputs.basis: Fully loaded ordinary-gift share for all dental work, not just painful teeth; judgment from new two-day dental service within broader medical clinic.

inputs.label: mental allocation
inputs.basis: Fully loaded ordinary-gift share for counseling and psychiatry; specialty spending not disclosed.

inputs.label: medical allocation
inputs.basis: General medical, chronic care, prescriptions and referral support; health left unquantified.

inputs.label: food other allocation
inputs.basis: Food pharmacy and remaining services; health left unquantified. All four shares sum to one.

inputs.label: dental episode cost
inputs.basis: Average fully loaded cost per nominal all-dental course, not only selected extraction. Target and non-target shares partition that activity; non-target budget feeds residual model without adding donor cost. Salary-oriented prior, not measured throughput.

inputs.label: mental course cost
inputs.basis: All-in mental-health course budget, independent prior: roughly eight funded/coordinated contacts at $150, including overhead and unsuccessful attempts; not clinic quote.

inputs.label: dental target
inputs.basis: Share of dental courses with severe pain and clinically indicated simple extraction; no credit to cleanings/exams/fillings here.

inputs.label: mental target
inputs.basis: Share of mental-health courses suitable for short-term counseling of depressive symptoms; exclude psychiatry-only and unsupported diagnoses.

inputs.label: dental completion
inputs.basis: Completed definitive care conditional on initiated target course; no credit to emergency exam alone.

inputs.label: mental completion
inputs.basis: Fraction reaching an adequate local counseling dose; full attempt costs retained.

inputs.label: dental unique
inputs.basis: Unique patient-period fraction; repeat teeth and repeat episodes excluded from additional utility summation.

inputs.label: mental disjoint
inputs.basis: Unique counseling patient-period fraction after excluding every dental-credited person and repeat courses; unknown linked-data prior.

inputs.label: dental capacity
inputs.basis: Maximum additional completed unique target patients in gift cohort; unverified capacity prior.

inputs.label: mental capacity
inputs.basis: Maximum additional completed disjoint counseling patients; unverified capacity prior.

inputs.label: dental utility
inputs.basis: Signed relief utility prior, loosely oriented by nonsignificant Swedish extraction before/after EQ5D .77 to .81; not a causal estimate.

inputs.label: dental resolution
inputs.basis: Successful pain resolution conditional on completed extraction, separate from course completion.

inputs.label: dental catchup
inputs.basis: Annual no-gift alternative-treatment/spontaneous symptom-resolution hazard, conditional on successful early treatment; central mean .25 years before hard cap.

inputs.label: dental horizon
inputs.basis: Hard maximum years of earlier relief after care begins, never lifetime.

inputs.label: dental delay
inputs.basis: Years until care starts; cohorts conditioned alive at start, delay discounts only.

inputs.label: dental harm
inputs.basis: Gift-date PV incremental procedural/tooth-function QALY loss per additional completed unique patient; net of eventual alternative-care harm.

inputs.label: mental utility
inputs.basis: Signed initial counseling utility advantage: independent prior, NOT Beck-score to EQ5D conversion.

inputs.label: mental fidelity
inputs.basis: Local effect-size transfer prior among adequate-dose completers; no claim clinic replicates trained trial therapists.

inputs.label: mental catchup
inputs.basis: Additional local alternative-care attenuation beyond imposed one-year fading; accounts for accessible public/free mental care.

inputs.label: mental horizon
inputs.basis: Counseling utility fades linearly to zero by one year after start; no residual lifetime mental-health benefit.

inputs.label: mental delay
inputs.basis: Care start delay, discounts only for an alive-at-start cohort.

inputs.label: mental harm
inputs.basis: Gift-date PV incremental burden/adverse effects per additional completed unique counseling patient; clinical deterioration already in signed utility excluded.

inputs.label: mortality
inputs.basis: Annual competing all-cause hazard during finite benefit, not a mortality reduction claim.

inputs.label: discount
inputs.basis: Continuous annual health discount rate.

inputs.label: bay share
inputs.basis: Direct Bay Area fraction; intended clinic catchment; no measured marginal residency split.

inputs.label: sf share
inputs.basis: Direct SF subset of Bay Area; weak prior from SF and San Mateo mission, not proof clinic location equals resident location.

inputs.label: volunteer resource per donor
inputs.basis: Additional gross associated volunteer opportunity-cost allowance per donor dollar, not a clinic valuation or incremental net cost.

inputs.label: external resource per donor
inputs.basis: Outside support for original dental/mental branches and common patient support only; BP/residual per-course allowances exclude these costs.

inputs.label: independent harm q
inputs.basis: Gift-date PV QALY loss independent of expanded care; separate from per-patient harms.

inputs.label: bp medical fraction
inputs.basis: General-medical budget fraction for HDFP-like hypertensive adults ages30–69/DBP≥90; unknown local case mix, not all visits.

inputs.label: bp course cost
inputs.basis: Fully loaded annual systematic-care cost: six contacts at$200 plus$300 drugs/labs; multiply by max(1,funded years), so longer care never costs only one year.

inputs.label: bp unique
inputs.basis: Unique annual patients after excluding dental/counseling patient-periods and repeats.

inputs.label: bp capacity
inputs.basis: Unverified additional unique annual-course capacity.

inputs.label: bp baseline hazard
inputs.basis: Current-care all-cause annual mortality prior near annualized HDFP referral arm, not untreated mortality.

inputs.label: bp relative hazard
inputs.basis: Constant-hazard approximation from HDFP5y risks6.4%stepped versus7.7%community referral; not observed first-year HR.

inputs.label: bp modern gap
inputs.basis: Remaining opportunity relative to historical referral comparator after modern public/free access, not fraction never treated.

inputs.label: bp delivery transfer
inputs.basis: Implementation relative to trial assignment effect; no second multiplication by absolute trial adherence.

inputs.label: bp active years
inputs.basis: Funded exposure; hazards equal comparator after this period.

inputs.label: bp latency
inputs.basis: Initial delay before any hazard effect within the funded exposure.

inputs.label: bp horizon
inputs.basis: Finite survival followup after care start; no permanent risk reduction.

inputs.label: bp delay
inputs.basis: Discount-only start delay, cohort alive at service start.

inputs.label: bp utility
inputs.basis: Utility among living high-risk cohort, independent prior.

inputs.label: bp harm
inputs.basis: Gift-date PV nonfatal incremental treatment harm; fatal effects already inside signed mortality contrast.

inputs.label: bp external per course
inputs.basis: Annual outside BP clinical/patient-time cost, multiplied by max(1,funded years); donor-paid and common original-branch support excluded.

inputs.label: residual unique
inputs.basis: Unique residual patient-periods after excluding all credited cohorts/repeats; full costs retained.

inputs.label: residual capacity
inputs.basis: Unknown additional unique annual-course capacity prior.

inputs.label: residual delay
inputs.basis: Discount-only delay; cohort alive at start.

inputs.label: residual harm
inputs.basis: Gift-date PV incremental harm outside signed utility, per additional unique course.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Weights are subjective elicited priors, not empirical frequencies. Central is not automatically the expectation. Preserve null/harm scenarios; never average ratios after dropping negative outcomes. Generic computational bounds are not credible intervals. A total impact claim beyond these direct-health mechanisms remains unwarranted.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2025 unaudited primary return has$1,183,897 PartIX expense including$291,013 depreciation plus$38,265 event directcost netted from revenue: combined$1,222,162. These are not a marginal quote or cashflow. Program$872,675,management$173,535,fundraising$137,687 do not disclose specialties. Whole$100K gift remains. BP donor/external annual costs scale with max(1,fundedyears). Residual course/external priors differ by group: acute$1,000/$100,chronic$1,500/$300,referral$3,000/$3,000,otherdental$600/$150,othermental$1,000/$200,food$800/$250. Outside categories exclude donor,volunteer and original-branch/common costs. Full gross associated cost is not a net societal ICER or exhaustive public-cost ledger; funds/food transfers are not automatically resource additions.

evidence.result: Extraction EQ5D mean .77 to .81 was nonsignificant (p=.297); the study lacks untreated access controls.
evidence.transfer: The .04 signed utility is a judgment, not a causal coefficient. Selected painful clinically indicated extraction only; no root-canal benefit transferred to an unavailable procedure.

evidence.design: Primary pragmatic randomized comparison with preference arms
evidence.population: 197 patients randomized among three arms; 464 total includes preference and therapy-only allocation
evidence.result: Brief counseling/CBT improved depression symptoms at four months, but groups converged by twelve months. GP psychological referral was held for four months.
evidence.transfer: A direction and short-duration anchor, not a QALY estimate. Utility is an independent prior, with a one-year fade, local fidelity attenuation and extra alternative-care catchup. No trial fidelity is assumed from generic short-term counseling availability.

evidence.design: Primary FY2025 IRS return, not audited accounts
evidence.result: Bundles service costs and confirms a broader medical home rather than a dental-only organization.
evidence.transfer: No specialty cash split or verified next-gift treatment plan. Annual report is linked but unreadable through available access; index counts are not used as a dated throughput denominator.

evidence.result: Healthy SF covers primary and mental-health care; routine dental is outside its covered service list.
evidence.transfer: Uninsured is not equivalent to no care. Funding replacement is separate from patient alternative-care catchup; eligibility, availability and waits still vary.

evidence.result: Systematic stepped care versus referral to community therapy: five-year all-cause mortality6.4% versus7.7%.
evidence.transfer: Current-care risk, modern gap, finite funded exposure/latency and relative implementation are explicit priors. Derived constant-hazard ratio is not an observed early effect. Trial assignment already incorporates adherence. No mortality double counting.

evidence.design: Explicit bounded health-state prior, not causal clinic evidence
evidence.population: Six disjoint named service groups, not generic remaining visits
evidence.result: Service-specific illness fractions, successful response, signed utility and catchup/horizon are separately exposed in99inputs. Clinical/referral completion and low food-related utility are not assumed uniform.
evidence.transfer: All numerical residual parameters remain weak priors; official menus support existence, not causal magnitude. No life-long disease-prevention award, generic starvation counterfactual or average visits×QALY. Measure mix and patient health, and retain null/adverse group stresses.

reservations: The mean is sensitive to elicited favorable-scenario probability and residual priors; neither numerical precision nor a passing calculator makes those probabilities evidence.

Current BP mortality is a selected-patient prior. HDFP is old and compared systematic care with existing community referral, not no treatment. Modern public access may eliminate the local treatment gap.
Residual morbidity is a coarse weak-prior branch for remaining direct care, not a multiplier fitted to a ranking threshold. Undocumented rare-event prevention may still matter.
Four cohorts are disjoint by assumptions, not linked data. Patient overlap and combined utility effects need direct validation.
Annual courses include unsuccessful and nonresponsive activity costs. Funded duration is finite; one year of donations does not buy lifelong medication adherence.
All harmful utility, treatment burden and mortality effects must remain signed without charging the same adverse outcome twice.
Government-free clinic financing does not mean government-free patient alternatives. Net public costs and savings remain unknown.
excludedBenefits: Additional fatal MI/stroke credit beyond BP all-cause survival
Unspecified perpetual prevention benefit from visits or education attendance
Net public savings and exhaustive downstream costs

comparisonBridge.headline: Subjective expectation-weight sensitivity
comparisonBridge.body: Favorable15% supplies 82.6%of meanQ. Subjective elicitation, not empirical frequencies: documented ongoing care and waiting demand put most mass on some added but partly replacing activity; central70% represents existing-provider alternatives and mixed clinical need. Favorable15% is a correlated high-need/volunteer-capacity state (severe case mix makes more targets and longer waits, available volunteer capacity lowers course cash cost), not independent success of every optimistic parameter. Cautious10% represents largely low-burden/already-served patients and weak effective delivery; structural null5% reserves complete displacement/no additional activity despite existing operation. These exact probabilities are judgment calls with no calibrated reference class; broad0–30% favorable-weight stress is required, and85%of meanhealth can come from15%tail. They are not evidence of specific funding room.
